thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: autoscaler-gpu-pool failed to provision capacity for pool 'inference-gpu-prod' (scale_up_attempts=3, reason=placement_failed). Paging @maya and @devon :rotating_light:

maya: seeing the same — queue depth spiking for realtime-gen route, token throttles kicking in. requests/sec -> 420/s, pending requests ~1.9k, average wait 6.2s and climbing.

devon: look like autoscaler hit max_retries and then gave up. logs show placement errors: 'MIG_BINPACK_FRAGMENTATION: insufficient contiguous MIG units', plus some MIG sizing mismatch warnings. attaching recent scheduler logs below.

maya: paste logs?

devon: ```
2028-05-14T12:02:07Z scheduler: allocate request for model=gpt-medium, seq_len=1024, required_mig=1g.10gb
2028-05-14T12:02:07Z scheduler: candidate nodes found=12, fitable=3
2028-05-14T12:02:07Z scheduler: placement failed on 3 nodes due to fragmentation: free_mig=[0.5g,0.25g,0.25g]
2028-05-14T12:02:08Z autoscaler: scale_up attempt 1 -> cloud request id=cr-53a, jobs queued=1200
2028-05-14T12:03:45Z autoscaler: scale_up attempt 2 -> placement_failed
2028-05-14T12:04:50Z autoscaler: scale_up attempt 3 -> placement_failed, giving up
```

kai: pinging — this smells like MIG partitioning mismatch since we recently rolled a node image that changed MIG profiles from {1g,2g,4g} to {0.5g,1g,2g}. a lot of nodes now have a bunch of 0.5g slices that can't serve 1g jobs.

henry: confirm: outstanding capacity exists but in smaller fragments, so binpacking fails and requests get stranded in the queue. cluster free GPUs reported 72% but effective available for 1g jobs is ~6%.

maya: customer-facing impact: realtime-gen latencies > 3s for ~30% of requests, some API errors 503 for routes using gpt-medium. Alice from CS, can you triage active customer escalations?

alice-cs: on it — informing 2 customers on paid Dedicated plans, giving ETA 30-45m. they asked for root cause once resolved.

devon: short-term mitigations we can try (ordered):
1) emergency fallback to smaller model variant that fits 0.5g MIG slices (gpt-medium-lite) — low-friction but quality hit.
2) temporarily relax model placement constraints to allow multi-slice packing (pack across two 0.5g MIGs for a single request) — risky, needs runtime change.
3) drain and reprovision a subset of nodes with larger MIG profiles (1g+) — takes ~12-18m per batch plus drain time.
4) manual eviction of non-critical batch jobs to free contiguous MIG groups.

maya: i'm leaning to (1) + (4) immediately. we need to stop customer-facing errors fast. (2) requires deploy window. (3) do in parallel targeting 5 nodes now.

kai: i can deploy the fallback routing in the router layer in ~6m: route gpt-medium requests to gpt-medium-lite for 10% sampled traffic initially, then ramp. will add header X-Redwood-Fallback for tracking.

henry: i'll start draining 6 highest-fragmentation nodes and reprovision with 1g MIG profile. giving estimates: each node drain + reprovision ~20m, so 6 nodes ~40m in parallel (cloud parallelism allows 3 at a time).

devon: manual batch job eviction: identify non-urgent batch pipelines tagged 'precompute:low' and evict. i see ~240 pending batch slots that map to contiguous MIG groups if freed. starting eviction now.

maya: start the on-call handoff at 12:35Z — i'm going offline for a meeting in 30m. @devon you'll be primary.

devon: acknowledged. I'll update incident status and coordinate with kai/henry.

[12:14] kai: router patch deployed to canary -> routing 15% traffic to gpt-medium-lite, metrics show immediate drop in queue depth by ~420 requests, p50 latency for fallback path 140ms, quality metric delta within acceptable thresholds for emergency.

[12:22] devon: batch eviction completed, freed capacity equivalent to 8 contiguous 1g MIGs. scheduler is now matching more placements. autoscaler retried and succeeded for 2 nodes.

[12:29] henry: first reprovisioned node back with 1g profile, scheduler reports fitable nodes increased from 3 to 9 for 1g jobs. queue drains steadily.

[12:34] maya: handoff: i'm signing out. devon you're oncall. escalation to eng-lead if we see error rate >5% sustained.

devon: continuing ops — status update to execs and CS in 10m. current state: queue length 420 -> trending down, error rate reduced from 4.8% -> 0.9%, autoscaler healthy after manual frees.

alice-cs: updated customers: two Dedicated customers notified we're mitigating with fallback models and expect full restoration in ~30-45m. both acknowledged.

[12:55] devon: followups for postmortem:
- investigate why node image change switched default MIG profiles without migration plan
- add autoscaler awareness of MIG fragmentation and smarter binpacking heuristics
- add a runbook for quick fallback routing to smaller model variants
- create metric for 'effective capacity by MIG class' surfaced in Console

maya: agree. please tag eng-runtime and eng-sre for followup. incident severity: sev3 (customer impact, partial outage for some routes).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: autoscaler and scheduler recovered, fallback routing rolled back. duration 41m.

devon: closing thread — will open a postmortem doc and link. good quick reaction everyone. :tada:
